newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds plow ahead, spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds plow ahead, spreads widen.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities remained sharply higher, but yield spreads to Treasuries were wider in late trade on Tuesday.

Two market-friendly reports on U.S. economic data sent Treasury prices surging more than a full point. Pass-through spreads widened sharply at first but recovered relatively well by late afternoon, traders said.
"We did pretty well today despite the sharp spike in (Treasury) paper," said one pass-through trader at a regional bank. He said there was better buying on the widening.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was up 15/32 at 101-01/32, yielding 105 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper rose 17/32 to 101-03/32, and Freddie Mac issues were up 19/32 at 101-12/32.
Five-year Treasuries were up 22/32 at 6.63 percent, and 10-year notes were up 33/32 at 6.76 percent.

The Labor Department reported the much-anticipated Employment Cost Index rose just 0.6 percent in the first quarter, much lower than the 0.9-percent consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters.
